units.function: Monolithic Feedback domain/service implementing Vote upsert, Company/global sharing preferences, target validation, local/shared payload snapshots, Issue/Agent/Skill/Instructions context capture, vendor-specific runtime-file reconstruction, trace queries and remote export state transitions.
units.dependencyDirection: The service directly depends on database tables, Agent Instructions, Run Log Store, filesystem/environment paths and Claude/Codex/OpenCode adapter parsers; routes and startup workers call it for both local feedback and external telemetry delivery.
units.keyDataModels: FeedbackVote and FeedbackExport, consent actor/time/terms, local_only/pending/sent/failed, Issue/comment/document target, Company/Agent/Run/cost/skill/instructions snapshots, adapter files, redaction summary, payload/bundle digests and export attempts.
units.lifecycle: Save validates an Agent-authored target, mutates Company and instance sharing state, upserts Vote/Export and builds a DB payload snapshot inside one transaction; flush selects pending/failed rows, reconstructs a fresh bundle from current DB/log/vendor files, uploads sequentially and then marks each row sent or failed.
units.testAssessment: The 1,155-line embedded-Postgres suite gives unusually strong behavior coverage for consent, non-retroactivity, target validity, sanitization examples and delivery states. Implementation-level gaps remain untested: no atomic row claim or multi-replica exclusion; no backoff/next-attempt/max/dead-letter; unscoped getById/getBundle and unbounded list; filesystem work inside the save transaction; unlimited file count and full-file reads before 10M-character truncation; shared global vendor homes; exact session ownership; mutable-source capture between consent and retry; canonical integrity completeness and authorization to change Company/global consent.
units.designRationale: Maximize diagnostic usefulness by automatically reconstructing rich provider-native execution context while keeping non-shared votes local and preserving durable export status.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a neutral DataEgress/Audit pipeline whose consent applies to an exact immutable byte manifest, not a later vendor-specific filesystem scrape.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as separate Feedback, ConsentPolicy, ExportManifest and DataEgressWorker application modules. Connector drivers may propose bounded artifacts through capability contracts, but Core stores an immutable consent-time manifest/digest, field/data-contract decisions and redaction receipt; worker atomically claims it and sends exactly those bytes with idempotency, retry schedule, dead-letter and delivery evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A board vote can change Company and instance-wide sharing state without service-level role authority. Export-time reconstruction reads mutable Run/log/vendor files after consent, so the approved payload and transmitted payload are not the same object. The bundle digest excludes most non-file fields, failure text is stored unsanitized, and shared local-board identity cannot establish an accountable human.
